title: Make Binary Decisions
core_invariant: Build one complete binary decision system before unpacking parts: baseline, split, classifier, predicted probabilities, default classification, confusion matrix, threshold changes, consequences. A threshold is policy, not an automatic property of the probability model.

stages.title: Frame the disengagement decision system
stages.instructions: Read the M09 invariant and the whole-first path: baseline → split → classifier → predicted probabilities → default classification → confusion matrix → threshold changes → consequences. The working case predicts whether a learner will disengage in the next 30 days (1 = event occurs). Data is synthetic; do not claim real-learner performance. Identify the evidence the gate will require: annotated system trace, split integrity, probability inspection, TP/TN/FP/FN accounting, metric comparison, accuracy-only failure diagnosis, consequence decision, learner-authored threshold ADR, calibration intuition, and a fresh no-AI threshold decision.

stages.title: Map probability model versus decision policy
stages.instructions: Annotate the baseline-to-consequence trace and mark the model versus threshold-policy boundary. Features map to estimated probability; probability plus threshold plus consequences/capacity map to action. If a threshold changes, decisions can change while learned coefficients and held-out probabilities stay fixed. Mark where test labels are forbidden during fit.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Map separates probability production from thresholded action and preserves the holdout boundary.

stages.title: Predict, execute, and move the threshold
stages.instructions: Complete the experiment cycle on the local learner-disengagement system. For every threshold or consequence experiment: (1) PREDICT the confusion-matrix cells, accuracy, precision, and recall, and which case IDs will cross the threshold. (2) COMMIT the prediction so it cannot be edited. (3) EXECUTE / RUN the comparison at 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, and 0.70 without refitting the probability model, after establishing the majority baseline and a stratified holdout. (4) OBSERVE TP, TN, FP, FN and metric tables with correct denominators. (5) SUBMIT an explanation referring to cases that crossed the threshold. Treat probability as a graded estimate, not a label or guarantee. Do not accept 0.50 merely because it is a library default.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Prediction is sealed before execute; confusion counts and precision/recall denominators are correct; threshold is treated as policy.

stages.title: Diagnose accurate-enough, harmful-by-default policy
stages.instructions: The seeded failure is a decision process, not a syntax error: the team accepts threshold 0.50 because it is the library-style default and reports only accuracy. It does not compare the majority baseline, inspect false negatives, or declare missed-disengagement consequences. On this imbalanced holdout, high accuracy can coexist with low recall. Diagnose before changing anything: compute the all-negative baseline; compute TP/TN/FP/FN at 0.50; state which cell is a learner who disengages with no outreach; compare metrics at 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, and 0.70; identify similar accuracy with different recall; declare FP and FN costs; compare total consequence cost; recommend a threshold and the operational trade-off. The repair is not always use a lower threshold; it is to treat threshold selection as explicit, reviewable policy.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Diagnosis shows accuracy-only reasoning concealing costly false negatives and repairs the policy with declared consequences.

stages.title: Author the threshold policy ADR
stages.instructions: Create a separate learner-authored ADR for the operating threshold. It must record the selected threshold and comparison rule, FP/FN cost assumptions, operating capacity, alternatives and rejected reasons, held-out evidence, accepted trade-offs, owner/status/date, monitoring, rollback, and measurable revisit triggers. The repository prompt remains unfilled. Notebook output alone does not satisfy the ADR requirement.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Learner-authored ADR governs the threshold with costs, capacity, alternatives, and revisit triggers.

stages.title: Fresh probability and threshold decision without assistance
stages.instructions: Complete this gate without AI-generated analysis or code and without reusing the notebook threshold table. A quality team assigns defect probabilities to eight batches A-H: 0.08, 0.19, 0.27, 0.36, 0.48, 0.59, 0.73, 0.88. Inspecting a good batch costs 2 units (FP); shipping a defective batch without inspection costs 9 units (FN); at most four batches can be inspected. Part A — commit before outcomes: define positive class 1, choose a threshold that respects capacity, list positive batches, predict how lowering the threshold affects FP/FN/precision/recall, and record why 0.50 is or is not appropriate. Part B — only after Part A, use outcomes A0 B0 C1 D0 E1 F0 G1 H1: compute TP/TN/FP/FN, accuracy, precision, recall, cost 2*FP+9*FN, compare with threshold 0.50, keep or revise, explain why a predicted probability is not a guarantee, and describe calibration evidence without naming a library. Arithmetic without a decision rationale is insufficient. Do not invent unseen training.

validation_rubric.pass_criteria: Committed pre-outcome policy, correct confusion accounting, capacity/consequence argument, and calibration explanation.

stages.title: Hand probabilities and policy to V02
stages.instructions: Explain how M09 adds the binary-decision path to V02: a probability-producing classifier plus an explicit probability-to-class policy. Hand off held-out probabilities, targets, candidate thresholds, TP/TN/FP/FN counts, and the threshold ADR to M10 without quietly changing the model or evaluation population. V02 must keep the probability model and the decision policy separable.

stages.title: Evaluate M09 evidence against the gate contract
stages.instructions: Evaluate submitted orientation, experiment, controlled-failure, ADR, and transfer evidence against the mission gate_contract. Issue PASSED when every required evidence item meets the pass threshold. Otherwise issue a targeted repair plan naming the failed stage, competency, artifact type, and knowledge node — do not force a full mission repeat.
